1	\section{Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	Under prompt-chain recursion ($\leq$32B), the $\theta$-invariant domain ordering arXiv ($\Kempirical{=}3$) $>$ C4 ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $=$ Code ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $>$ Wikipedia ($\Kempirical{=}1$) holds across 7/9 continuation-mode configurations (4/6 families); multi-source pooling preserves domain-calibrated ceilings across all four domains.
5	DeBERTa matches OBD on low-complexity domains but extends $\Kempirical$ by $+1$ on Wikipedia and arXiv (two-tier ceiling).
6	$\Kempirical$ localizes where depth-aware curation yields diminishing returns; retrain-chain experiments confirm $\Kempirical{\geq}4$ across three families, and scaling beyond 32B remains open.
7

1	\section{Method}
2	\label{sec:method}
3	
4	\subsection{Problem Formulation}
5	\label{sec:formulation}
6	
7	A generation operator $G_\delta$ (LLM + decoding strategy $\delta$) produces successive generations $X \to Y_1 \to \cdots \to Y_K$, where $Y_k = G_\delta(Y_{k-1})$ and $Y_0 \triangleq X$ (Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).
8	This sequence forms a Markov chain.
9	By the Data Processing Inequality, $I(X; Y_1) \geq I(X; Y_2) \geq \cdots \geq 0$: the original signal degrades monotonically.
10	Together with Markov chain convergence, this motivates a finite $\Ktheory$ beyond which adjacent generations become indistinguishable; DPI guarantees existence but does not bound $\Ktheory$, so the actual saturation depth must be measured empirically.
11	
12	We define the operational lower bound $K^*_{\text{empirical}}$ (hereafter $\Kempirical$):
13	\begin{equation}
14	  \Kempirical = \max\!\bigl\{k \!\geq\! 1 : \mathrm{CI}_{\mathrm{low}}(\auc_{j\text{-}1,j}) > \theta,\ \forall j \!\leq\! k\bigr\},
15	  \label{eq:kstar}
16	\end{equation}
17	where $\mathrm{CI}_{\mathrm{low}}(\auc_{k-1,k})$ is the lower bound of a 95\% bootstrap confidence interval (1{,}000 resamples\footnote{Boundary-pair results in Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci} use 1{,}000 resamples; arXiv cross-scorer CIs (Table~\ref{tab:arxiv_crossscorer_ci}) use 10{,}000 for tighter bounds at the margin.}) over the pairwise AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) between depths $k{-}1$ and $k$, and $\theta = 0.60$ is a post-hoc operational threshold (motivated below).
18	This criterion ensures that $\Kempirical$ reflects statistically robust discriminability rather than sampling noise; the $\forall j \leq k$ constraint is naturally satisfied because $\auc_{k,k+1}$ decreases monotonically for all pairs above $\theta$ across all tested configurations; negligible fluctuations ($\Delta < 0.02$) occur only at deeper depths where discrimination approaches chance level (Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci}).
19	Since 0v1 $\auc > \theta$ in all tested configurations, $\Kempirical \geq 1$; $\Kempirical{=}0$ (undetectable first-generation text) is not observed.
20	$\Kempirical$ is an operational quantity jointly conditioned on the feature set and threshold $\theta$; the domain ordering is stable across $\theta \in [0.575, 0.65]$ (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}), though absolute $\Kempirical$ values shift with $\theta$.
21	We additionally verify that non-boundary-pair CI upper bounds fall below $\theta$ (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}).
22	
23	\paragraph{Threshold choice.}
24	We set $\theta{=}0.60$ as a post-hoc operational threshold, chosen at the empirical discontinuity in the AUC distribution (Figure~\ref{fig:kstar_theta}).
25	A 10{,}000-iteration permutation test yields a 95th-percentile null of ${<}\,0.55$ and $p < 0.002$ for all boundary comparisons, placing $\theta{=}0.60$ well above the empirical null.
26	$\Kempirical{=}2$ is stable across $\theta \in [0.55, 0.65]$ for all but two marginal configurations (Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci_extended}): 1v2 AUC values cluster at $0.61$--$0.70$ while 2v3 values cluster at $0.55$--$0.59$, creating a ${\sim}$5--11\,pp discontinuity.
27	Only at extremes does $\Kempirical$ shift: $\theta{=}0.55$ yields $\Kempirical{=}3$ for two Qwen configurations; $\theta{=}0.70$ yields $\Kempirical{=}1$ across all configurations.
28	The downstream filtering evaluation (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}) uses the OBD classifier without re-optimizing $\theta$, avoiding circularity.
29	A leave-one-family-out (LOFO) cross-validation on C4 provides an internal consistency check (not external validation): each of five folds derives $\hat{\theta}$ from the gap midpoint between $\min(\auc_{1v2})$ and $\max(\auc_{2v3})$ over the remaining families, yielding $\hat{\theta} \in [0.5725, 0.6004]$; $\theta{=}0.60$ falls within this range, and 8/9 held-out predictions match the original $\Kempirical$ (the single mismatch is the borderline rewrite-mode configuration; Table~\ref{tab:theta_lofo}).
30	ArXiv corroborates with 6/6 LOFO agreement; Wikipedia is underdetermined because most models produce near-chance 1v2 AUC, invalidating the gap-based derivation (Appendix~\ref{sec:theta_lofo}).
31	
32	
33	\subsection{Features and Classifier}
34	\label{sec:features}
35	
36	Each document is characterized by a 15-dimensional feature vector spanning four groups: \emph{surprisal moments} (mean, std, skewness, kurtosis; 4~dims), \emph{surprisal derivatives} (mean and std of first- and second-order differences, plus first-order skewness; 5~dims), \emph{vocabulary diversity} (type-token ratio, hapax legomena ratio, self-BLEU; 3~dims), and \emph{frequency tail statistics} (frequency kurtosis, entropy, rare token fraction; 3~dims).
37	All features are computed from token-level surprisal values via an external scorer model (full definitions in Table~\ref{tab:s5_features}, Appendix).
38	Self-BLEU is computed within each CV fold using only same-fold, same-depth reference samples to prevent leakage; it ranks \#1 in 1/8 conditions (greedy decoding) but is absent from the top-3 in all 7 others.
39	Removing self-BLEU reduces mean $\auc_{1v2}$ by $< 1$\,pp across all models (14D $\Kempirical = 2$ for all 4 configurations; bootstrap CIs in Table~\ref{tab:selfbleu_ablation}); in deployment where depth labels are unavailable, self-BLEU can be replaced with corpus-level self-similarity or omitted with minimal performance loss.
40	Hand-crafted features enable cross-generator transfer without retraining and permit attribution of discriminative power to specific text properties.
41	
42	We use \emph{Ordinal Binary Decomposition} (OBD), decomposing the $(K{+}1)$-class problem into $K$ cumulative binary sub-classifiers, each estimating $P(\text{depth} > k \mid \mathbf{x})$ via LightGBM~\cite{ke2017lightgbm} (hyperparameters in Table~\ref{tab:s6_lgbm_params}).
43	OBD achieves lower MAE than multiclass LightGBM (e.g., 0.984 vs.\ 1.016 on Qwen-rewrite) while maintaining superior pairwise $\auc$ (mean 0.6095 vs.\ 0.4883 for ordinal logistic regression).
44	
45	\subsection{Experimental Setup}
46	\label{sec:experimental_setup}
47	
48	We evaluate ten configurations spanning six architecture families (Table~\ref{tab:setup}): Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (rewrite and continuation modes), Qwen2.5-1.5B (base, continuation), Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-14B, Pythia-1.4B, OLMo-1B, Gemma-2-2B, LLaMA-3.1-8B, and Mistral-7B (all continuation except Qwen-rw).
49	Each uses 5{,}000 C4~\cite{raffel2020t5} seeds truncated to 256 tokens, recursively generated for $K{=}5$ iterations (30{,}000 documents per configuration).
50	Default decoding: nucleus $p{=}0.95$, $T{=}1.0$; decoding ablation covers greedy, $T{=}0.7$, and $T{=}1.2$.
51	Continuation mode truncates seeds to 128 tokens and extends to 256; rewrite mode paraphrases the full text.
52	Evaluation: 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation grouped by seed document; pairwise $\auc$ as primary metric.
53

55	\centering
56	\small
57	\caption{Experimental configurations for depth-chain generation. \textbf{Config}: shorthand identifier; \textbf{Model}: architecture and parameter count; \textbf{Mode}: generation strategy (continuation or rewrite); $N$: number of seed documents per depth level.}
58	\label{tab:setup}
59	\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
60	\begin{tabular}{llcc}
61	\toprule
62	\textbf{Config} & \textbf{Model} & \textbf{Mode} & $N$ \\
63	\midrule
64	Qwen-rw   & Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct & Rewrite & 5{,}000 \\
65	Qwen-cont & Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\
66	Qwen-base & Qwen2.5-1.5B          & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\
67	Pythia    & Pythia-1.4B            & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\
68	OLMo      & OLMo-1B               & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\

\section{Method}
\label{sec:method}

\subsection{Problem Formulation}
\label{sec:formulation}

A generation operator $G_\delta$ (LLM + decoding strategy $\delta$) produces successive generations $X \to Y_1 \to \cdots \to Y_K$, where $Y_k = G_\delta(Y_{k-1})$ and $Y_0 \triangleq X$ (Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).
This sequence forms a Markov chain.
By the Data Processing Inequality, $I(X; Y_1) \geq I(X; Y_2) \geq \cdots \geq 0$: the original signal degrades monotonically.
Together with Markov chain convergence, this motivates a finite $\Ktheory$ beyond which adjacent generations become indistinguishable; DPI guarantees existence but does not bound $\Ktheory$, so the actual saturation depth must be measured empirically.

We define the operational lower bound $K^*_{\text{empirical}}$ (hereafter $\Kempirical$):
\begin{equation}
  \Kempirical = \max\!\bigl\{k \!\geq\! 1 : \mathrm{CI}_{\mathrm{low}}(\auc_{j\text{-}1,j}) > \theta,\ \forall j \!\leq\! k\bigr\},
  \label{eq:kstar}
\end{equation}
where $\mathrm{CI}_{\mathrm{low}}(\auc_{k-1,k})$ is the lower bound of a 95\% bootstrap confidence interval (1{,}000 resamples\footnote{Boundary-pair results in Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci} use 1{,}000 resamples; arXiv cross-scorer CIs (Table~\ref{tab:arxiv_crossscorer_ci}) use 10{,}000 for tighter bounds at the margin.}) over the pairwise AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) between depths $k{-}1$ and $k$, and $\theta = 0.60$ is a post-hoc operational threshold (motivated below).
This criterion ensures that $\Kempirical$ reflects statistically robust discriminability rather than sampling noise; the $\forall j \leq k$ constraint is naturally satisfied because $\auc_{k,k+1}$ decreases monotonically for all pairs above $\theta$ across all tested configurations; negligible fluctuations ($\Delta < 0.02$) occur only at deeper depths where discrimination approaches chance level (Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci}).
Since 0v1 $\auc > \theta$ in all tested configurations, $\Kempirical \geq 1$; $\Kempirical{=}0$ (undetectable first-generation text) is not observed.
$\Kempirical$ is an operational quantity jointly conditioned on the feature set and threshold $\theta$; the domain ordering is stable across $\theta \in [0.575, 0.65]$ (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}), though absolute $\Kempirical$ values shift with $\theta$.
We additionally verify that non-boundary-pair CI upper bounds fall below $\theta$ (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}).

\paragraph{Threshold choice.}
We set $\theta{=}0.60$ as a post-hoc operational threshold, chosen at the empirical discontinuity in the AUC distribution (Figure~\ref{fig:kstar_theta}).
A 10{,}000-iteration permutation test yields a 95th-percentile null of ${<}\,0.55$ and $p < 0.002$ for all boundary comparisons, placing $\theta{=}0.60$ well above the empirical null.
$\Kempirical{=}2$ is stable across $\theta \in [0.55, 0.65]$ for all but two marginal configurations (Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci_extended}): 1v2 AUC values cluster at $0.61$--$0.70$ while 2v3 values cluster at $0.55$--$0.59$, creating a ${\sim}$5--11\,pp discontinuity.
Only at extremes does $\Kempirical$ shift: $\theta{=}0.55$ yields $\Kempirical{=}3$ for two Qwen configurations; $\theta{=}0.70$ yields $\Kempirical{=}1$ across all configurations.
The downstream filtering evaluation (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}) uses the OBD classifier without re-optimizing $\theta$, avoiding circularity.
A leave-one-family-out (LOFO) cross-validation on C4 provides an internal consistency check (not external validation): each of five folds derives $\hat{\theta}$ from the gap midpoint between $\min(\auc_{1v2})$ and $\max(\auc_{2v3})$ over the remaining families, yielding $\hat{\theta} \in [0.5725, 0.6004]$; $\theta{=}0.60$ falls within this range, and 8/9 held-out predictions match the original $\Kempirical$ (the single mismatch is the borderline rewrite-mode configuration; Table~\ref{tab:theta_lofo}).
ArXiv corroborates with 6/6 LOFO agreement; Wikipedia is underdetermined because most models produce near-chance 1v2 AUC, invalidating the gap-based derivation (Appendix~\ref{sec:theta_lofo}).


\subsection{Features and Classifier}
\label{sec:features}

Each document is characterized by a 15-dimensional feature vector spanning four groups: \emph{surprisal moments} (mean, std, skewness, kurtosis; 4~dims), \emph{surprisal derivatives} (mean and std of first- and second-order differences, plus first-order skewness; 5~dims), \emph{vocabulary diversity} (type-token ratio, hapax legomena ratio, self-BLEU; 3~dims), and \emph{frequency tail statistics} (frequency kurtosis, entropy, rare token fraction; 3~dims).
All features are computed from token-level surprisal values via an external scorer model (full definitions in Table~\ref{tab:s5_features}, Appendix).
Self-BLEU is computed within each CV fold using only same-fold, same-depth reference samples to prevent leakage; it ranks \#1 in 1/8 conditions (greedy decoding) but is absent from the top-3 in all 7 others.
Removing self-BLEU reduces mean $\auc_{1v2}$ by $< 1$\,pp across all models (14D $\Kempirical = 2$ for all 4 configurations; bootstrap CIs in Table~\ref{tab:selfbleu_ablation}); in deployment where depth labels are unavailable, self-BLEU can be replaced with corpus-level self-similarity or omitted with minimal performance loss.
Hand-crafted features enable cross-generator transfer without retraining and permit attribution of discriminative power to specific text properties.

We use \emph{Ordinal Binary Decomposition} (OBD), decomposing the $(K{+}1)$-class problem into $K$ cumulative binary sub-classifiers, each estimating $P(\text{depth} > k \mid \mathbf{x})$ via LightGBM~\cite{ke2017lightgbm} (hyperparameters in Table~\ref{tab:s6_lgbm_params}).
OBD achieves lower MAE than multiclass LightGBM (e.g., 0.984 vs.\ 1.016 on Qwen-rewrite) while maintaining superior pairwise $\auc$ (mean 0.6095 vs.\ 0.4883 for ordinal logistic regression).

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:experimental_setup}

We evaluate ten configurations spanning six architecture families (Table~\ref{tab:setup}): Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (rewrite and continuation modes), Qwen2.5-1.5B (base, continuation), Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-14B, Pythia-1.4B, OLMo-1B, Gemma-2-2B, LLaMA-3.1-8B, and Mistral-7B (all continuation except Qwen-rw).
Each uses 5{,}000 C4~\cite{raffel2020t5} seeds truncated to 256 tokens, recursively generated for $K{=}5$ iterations (30{,}000 documents per configuration).
Default decoding: nucleus $p{=}0.95$, $T{=}1.0$; decoding ablation covers greedy, $T{=}0.7$, and $T{=}1.2$.
Continuation mode truncates seeds to 128 tokens and extends to 256; rewrite mode paraphrases the full text.
Evaluation: 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation grouped by seed document; pairwise $\auc$ as primary metric.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Experimental configurations for depth-chain generation. \textbf{Config}: shorthand identifier; \textbf{Model}: architecture and parameter count; \textbf{Mode}: generation strategy (continuation or rewrite); $N$: number of seed documents per depth level.}
\label{tab:setup}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{llcc}
\toprule
\textbf{Config} & \textbf{Model} & \textbf{Mode} & $N$ \\
\midrule
Qwen-rw   & Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct & Rewrite & 5{,}000 \\
Qwen-cont & Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\
Qwen-base & Qwen2.5-1.5B          & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\
Pythia    & Pythia-1.4B            & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\
OLMo      & OLMo-1B               & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\
Gemma     & Gemma-2-2B            & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\
Qwen-7B   & Qwen2.5-7B            & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\
Qwen-14B  & Qwen2.5-14B           & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\
LLaMA-8B  & LLaMA-3.1-8B          & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\
Mistral   & Mistral-7B            & Continuation & 5{,}000 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\end{table}

1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:introduction}
3	
4	Web-scale text corpora are increasingly contaminated by synthetic content that has itself been generated from earlier synthetic content.
5	Estimates suggest that a substantial fraction of online text is machine-generated~\cite{sun2025aigt, spennemann2025quantifying}, and this share continues to rise.
6	When synthetic text is recursively fed back as input, the resulting multi-generational content degrades with each iteration: tail modes vanish, lexical diversity contracts, and surprisal distributions flatten~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, dohmatob2024model}.
7	This degradation arises in both \emph{retrain-chains} (iteratively training on model outputs) and \emph{prompt-chains} (recursively prompting a fixed model to generate from its own prior outputs); we study prompt-chains, which isolate text-intrinsic information loss from training dynamics (Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_limitations}).
8	Yet the dominant paradigm treats all machine-generated text identically and ignores the generational depth dimension.
9	
10	\begin{figure*}[t]
11	\centering
12	\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/pipeline.pdf}
13	\caption{Generational depth estimation pipeline. Seed documents are recursively passed through a generation operator $G_\delta$ to produce a depth chain. Statistical features are fed to the OBD-LightGBM classifier for depth prediction.}
14	\label{fig:pipeline}
15	\end{figure*}
16	
17	This gap cuts across multiple communities.
18	Binary detectors~\cite{basani2026diveye, zhang2024minkpp} produce no depth estimate (Section~\ref{sec:binary_confidence}).
19	Membership inference~\cite{zawalski2026codec} addresses a different question, and the model collapse literature~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, alemohammad2024selfconsuming, schaeffer2025position} provides no per-text tool.
20	Data selection methods~\cite{xie2023dsir, tirumala2023d4, drayson2025} likewise ignore recursive depth.
21	No existing method estimates how many rounds of recursive generation a text has undergone.
22	
23	Knowing whether the discriminable depth is finite, and where it saturates, has direct practical consequences.
24	For data curation, the saturation point determines filtering granularity: if discrimination collapses at depth 2, graduated weighting beyond that boundary injects noise, and binary filtering becomes the principled choice.
25	Model collapse theory predicts monotonic quality degradation across generations, but existing analyses are population-level and provide no per-text measure of where degradation saturates.
26	$\Kempirical$ fills this gap by localizing the generation at which adjacent outputs become empirically indistinguishable.
27	
28	The Data Processing Inequality implies that information degrades monotonically across generations, motivating a finite discrimination boundary $\Kstar$; its actual value is determined empirically.
29	We present an empirical characterization study that formalizes $\Kempirical$ (the maximum depth at which a classifier reliably distinguishes adjacent generations) and measures it under prompt-chain generation using 15 statistical features computed via a fixed reference scorer (Section~\ref{sec:features}) and an Ordinal Binary Decomposition (OBD) LightGBM classifier.
30	We operationalize $\Kempirical$ as the deepest $k \geq 1$ where the pairwise $\auc_{k-1,k}$ exceeds $\theta = 0.60$ (Section~\ref{sec:formulation}).
31	
32	Our contributions:
33	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
34	  \item \textbf{First empirical measurement of $\Kempirical$} across 10 model configurations (6 architecture families, 1B--14B), 4 source domains (3 text + 1 code), and 4 decoding strategies at $\theta{=}0.60$: 4/6 families (7/9 continuation-mode configurations) yield $\Kempirical{=}2$ on C4 ($p \leq 0.002$; Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}); multi-source pooling preserves domain-calibrated $\Kempirical$ across all four domains ($+0.008$ $\auc$ for generator identity).
35	  Zero-shot frontier LLMs likewise collapse beyond $\Kempirical$: per-depth recall at depths $\geq 2$ ranges from 8--38\% (vs.\ 20\% chance), indicating error redistribution rather than genuine depth recovery (Section~\ref{sec:why_kstar}).
36	  \item \textbf{Domain ordering}: arXiv ($\Kempirical{=}3$) $>$ C4 ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $=$ Code ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $>$ Wikipedia ($\Kempirical{=}1$) holds across tested configurations; code (Python) matches web text depth despite a different modality, confirmed by multi-source pooling (Section~\ref{sec:cross_domain}).
37	  \item \textbf{Transfer and consistency check}: largely generator-independent features within continuation mode enable 80--92\% accuracy retention among tested configurations ($\rho > 0.90$; Section~\ref{sec:transfer}), though boundary-level $\Kempirical$ assignments are fragile under cross-model transfer (4/6 off-diagonal 7B pairs fall below $\theta$); as a consistency check, domain-appropriate $\Kempirical$ correctly predicts binary ${>}$ graduated filtering for web text (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}).
38	\end{enumerate}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Web-scale text corpora are increasingly contaminated by synthetic content that has itself been generated from earlier synthetic content.
Estimates suggest that a substantial fraction of online text is machine-generated~\cite{sun2025aigt, spennemann2025quantifying}, and this share continues to rise.
When synthetic text is recursively fed back as input, the resulting multi-generational content degrades with each iteration: tail modes vanish, lexical diversity contracts, and surprisal distributions flatten~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, dohmatob2024model}.
This degradation arises in both \emph{retrain-chains} (iteratively training on model outputs) and \emph{prompt-chains} (recursively prompting a fixed model to generate from its own prior outputs); we study prompt-chains, which isolate text-intrinsic information loss from training dynamics (Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_limitations}).
Yet the dominant paradigm treats all machine-generated text identically and ignores the generational depth dimension.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/pipeline.pdf}
\caption{Generational depth estimation pipeline. Seed documents are recursively passed through a generation operator $G_\delta$ to produce a depth chain. Statistical features are fed to the OBD-LightGBM classifier for depth prediction.}
\label{fig:pipeline}
\end{figure*}

This gap cuts across multiple communities.
Binary detectors~\cite{basani2026diveye, zhang2024minkpp} produce no depth estimate (Section~\ref{sec:binary_confidence}).
Membership inference~\cite{zawalski2026codec} addresses a different question, and the model collapse literature~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, alemohammad2024selfconsuming, schaeffer2025position} provides no per-text tool.
Data selection methods~\cite{xie2023dsir, tirumala2023d4, drayson2025} likewise ignore recursive depth.
No existing method estimates how many rounds of recursive generation a text has undergone.

Knowing whether the discriminable depth is finite, and where it saturates, has direct practical consequences.
For data curation, the saturation point determines filtering granularity: if discrimination collapses at depth 2, graduated weighting beyond that boundary injects noise, and binary filtering becomes the principled choice.
Model collapse theory predicts monotonic quality degradation across generations, but existing analyses are population-level and provide no per-text measure of where degradation saturates.
$\Kempirical$ fills this gap by localizing the generation at which adjacent outputs become empirically indistinguishable.

The Data Processing Inequality implies that information degrades monotonically across generations, motivating a finite discrimination boundary $\Kstar$; its actual value is determined empirically.
We present an empirical characterization study that formalizes $\Kempirical$ (the maximum depth at which a classifier reliably distinguishes adjacent generations) and measures it under prompt-chain generation using 15 statistical features computed via a fixed reference scorer (Section~\ref{sec:features}) and an Ordinal Binary Decomposition (OBD) LightGBM classifier.
We operationalize $\Kempirical$ as the deepest $k \geq 1$ where the pairwise $\auc_{k-1,k}$ exceeds $\theta = 0.60$ (Section~\ref{sec:formulation}).

Our contributions:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
  \item \textbf{First empirical measurement of $\Kempirical$} across 10 model configurations (6 architecture families, 1B--14B), 4 source domains (3 text + 1 code), and 4 decoding strategies at $\theta{=}0.60$: 4/6 families (7/9 continuation-mode configurations) yield $\Kempirical{=}2$ on C4 ($p \leq 0.002$; Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}); multi-source pooling preserves domain-calibrated $\Kempirical$ across all four domains ($+0.008$ $\auc$ for generator identity).
  Zero-shot frontier LLMs likewise collapse beyond $\Kempirical$: per-depth recall at depths $\geq 2$ ranges from 8--38\% (vs.\ 20\% chance), indicating error redistribution rather than genuine depth recovery (Section~\ref{sec:why_kstar}).
  \item \textbf{Domain ordering}: arXiv ($\Kempirical{=}3$) $>$ C4 ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $=$ Code ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $>$ Wikipedia ($\Kempirical{=}1$) holds across tested configurations; code (Python) matches web text depth despite a different modality, confirmed by multi-source pooling (Section~\ref{sec:cross_domain}).
  \item \textbf{Transfer and consistency check}: largely generator-independent features within continuation mode enable 80--92\% accuracy retention among tested configurations ($\rho > 0.90$; Section~\ref{sec:transfer}), though boundary-level $\Kempirical$ assignments are fragile under cross-model transfer (4/6 off-diagonal 7B pairs fall below $\theta$); as a consistency check, domain-appropriate $\Kempirical$ correctly predicts binary ${>}$ graduated filtering for web text (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}).
\end{enumerate}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Web-scale text corpora are increasingly contaminated by synthetic content that has itself been generated from earlier synthetic content.
Estimates suggest that a substantial fraction of online text is machine-generated~\cite{sun2025aigt, spennemann2025quantifying}, and this share continues to rise.
When synthetic text is recursively fed back as input, the resulting multi-generational content degrades with each iteration: tail modes vanish, lexical diversity contracts, and surprisal distributions flatten~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, dohmatob2024model}.
This degradation arises in both \emph{retrain-chains} (iteratively training on model outputs) and \emph{prompt-chains} (recursively prompting a fixed model to generate from its own prior outputs); we study prompt-chains, which isolate text-intrinsic information loss from training dynamics (Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_limitations}).
Yet the dominant paradigm treats all machine-generated text identically and ignores the generational depth dimension.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/pipeline.pdf}
\caption{Generational depth estimation pipeline. Seed documents are recursively passed through a generation operator $G_\delta$ to produce a depth chain. Statistical features are fed to the OBD-LightGBM classifier for depth prediction.}
\label{fig:pipeline}
\end{figure*}

This gap cuts across multiple communities.
Binary detectors~\cite{basani2026diveye, zhang2024minkpp} produce no depth estimate (Section~\ref{sec:binary_confidence}).
Membership inference~\cite{zawalski2026codec} addresses a different question, and the model collapse literature~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, alemohammad2024selfconsuming, schaeffer2025position} provides no per-text tool.
Data selection methods~\cite{xie2023dsir, tirumala2023d4, drayson2025} likewise ignore recursive depth.
No existing method estimates how many rounds of recursive generation a text has undergone.

Knowing whether the discriminable depth is finite, and where it saturates, has direct practical consequences.
For data curation, the saturation point determines filtering granularity: if discrimination collapses at depth 2, graduated weighting beyond that boundary injects noise, and binary filtering becomes the principled choice.
Model collapse theory predicts monotonic quality degradation across generations, but existing analyses are population-level and provide no per-text measure of where degradation saturates.
$\Kempirical$ fills this gap by localizing the generation at which adjacent outputs become empirically indistinguishable.

The Data Processing Inequality implies that information degrades monotonically across generations, motivating a finite discrimination boundary $\Kstar$; its actual value is determined empirically.
We present an empirical characterization study that formalizes $\Kempirical$ (the maximum depth at which a classifier reliably distinguishes adjacent generations) and measures it under prompt-chain generation using 15 statistical features computed via a fixed reference scorer (Section~\ref{sec:features}) and an Ordinal Binary Decomposition (OBD) LightGBM classifier.
We operationalize $\Kempirical$ as the deepest $k \geq 1$ where the pairwise $\auc_{k-1,k}$ exceeds $\theta = 0.60$ (Section~\ref{sec:formulation}).

Our contributions:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
  \item \textbf{First empirical measurement of $\Kempirical$} across 10 model configurations (6 architecture families, 1B--14B), 4 source domains (3 text + 1 code), and 4 decoding strategies at $\theta{=}0.60$: 4/6 families (7/9 continuation-mode configurations) yield $\Kempirical{=}2$ on C4 ($p \leq 0.002$; Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}); multi-source pooling preserves domain-calibrated $\Kempirical$ across all four domains ($+0.008$ $\auc$ for generator identity).
  Zero-shot frontier LLMs likewise collapse beyond $\Kempirical$: per-depth recall at depths $\geq 2$ ranges from 8--38\% (vs.\ 20\% chance), indicating error redistribution rather than genuine depth recovery (Section~\ref{sec:why_kstar}).
  \item \textbf{Domain ordering}: arXiv ($\Kempirical{=}3$) $>$ C4 ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $=$ Code ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $>$ Wikipedia ($\Kempirical{=}1$) holds across tested configurations; code (Python) matches web text depth despite a different modality, confirmed by multi-source pooling (Section~\ref{sec:cross_domain}).
  \item \textbf{Transfer and consistency check}: largely generator-independent features within continuation mode enable 80--92\% accuracy retention among tested configurations ($\rho > 0.90$; Section~\ref{sec:transfer}), though boundary-level $\Kempirical$ assignments are fragile under cross-model transfer (4/6 off-diagonal 7B pairs fall below $\theta$); as a consistency check, domain-appropriate $\Kempirical$ correctly predicts binary ${>}$ graduated filtering for web text (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}).
\end{enumerate}

\section{Method}
\label{sec:method}

\subsection{Problem Formulation}
\label{sec:formulation}

A generation operator $G_\delta$ (LLM + decoding strategy $\delta$) produces successive generations $X \to Y_1 \to \cdots \to Y_K$, where $Y_k = G_\delta(Y_{k-1})$ and $Y_0 \triangleq X$ (Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).
This sequence forms a Markov chain.
By the Data Processing Inequality, $I(X; Y_1) \geq I(X; Y_2) \geq \cdots \geq 0$: the original signal degrades monotonically.
Together with Markov chain convergence, this motivates a finite $\Ktheory$ beyond which adjacent generations become indistinguishable; DPI guarantees existence but does not bound $\Ktheory$, so the actual saturation depth must be measured empirically.

We define the operational lower bound $K^*_{\text{empirical}}$ (hereafter $\Kempirical$):
\begin{equation}
  \Kempirical = \max\!\bigl\{k \!\geq\! 1 : \mathrm{CI}_{\mathrm{low}}(\auc_{j\text{-}1,j}) > \theta,\ \forall j \!\leq\! k\bigr\},
  \label{eq:kstar}
\end{equation}
where $\mathrm{CI}_{\mathrm{low}}(\auc_{k-1,k})$ is the lower bound of a 95\% bootstrap confidence interval (1{,}000 resamples\footnote{Boundary-pair results in Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci} use 1{,}000 resamples; arXiv cross-scorer CIs (Table~\ref{tab:arxiv_crossscorer_ci}) use 10{,}000 for tighter bounds at the margin.}) over the pairwise AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) between depths $k{-}1$ and $k$, and $\theta = 0.60$ is a post-hoc operational threshold (motivated below).
This criterion ensures that $\Kempirical$ reflects statistically robust discriminability rather than sampling noise; the $\forall j \leq k$ constraint is naturally satisfied because $\auc_{k,k+1}$ decreases monotonically for all pairs above $\theta$ across all tested configurations; negligible fluctuations ($\Delta < 0.02$) occur only at deeper depths where discrimination approaches chance level (Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci}).
Since 0v1 $\auc > \theta$ in all tested configurations, $\Kempirical \geq 1$; $\Kempirical{=}0$ (undetectable first-generation text) is not observed.
$\Kempirical$ is an operational quantity jointly conditioned on the feature set and threshold $\theta$; the domain ordering is stable across $\theta \in [0.575, 0.65]$ (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}), though absolute $\Kempirical$ values shift with $\theta$.
We additionally verify that non-boundary-pair CI upper bounds fall below $\theta$ (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}).

\paragraph{Threshold choice.}
We set $\theta{=}0.60$ as a post-hoc operational threshold, chosen at the empirical discontinuity in the AUC distribution (Figure~\ref{fig:kstar_theta}).
A 10{,}000-iteration permutation test yields a 95th-percentile null of ${<}\,0.55$ and $p < 0.002$ for all boundary comparisons, placing $\theta{=}0.60$ well above the empirical null.
$\Kempirical{=}2$ is stable across $\theta \in [0.55, 0.65]$ for all but two marginal configurations (Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci_extended}): 1v2 AUC values cluster at $0.61$--$0.70$ while 2v3 values cluster at $0.55$--$0.59$, creating a ${\sim}$5--11\,pp discontinuity.
Only at extremes does $\Kempirical$ shift: $\theta{=}0.55$ yields $\Kempirical{=}3$ for two Qwen configurations; $\theta{=}0.70$ yields $\Kempirical{=}1$ across all configurations.
The downstream filtering evaluation (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}) uses the OBD classifier without re-optimizing $\theta$, avoiding circularity.
A leave-one-family-out (LOFO) cross-validation on C4 provides an internal consistency check (not external validation): each of five folds derives $\hat{\theta}$ from the gap midpoint between $\min(\auc_{1v2})$ and $\max(\auc_{2v3})$ over the remaining families, yielding $\hat{\theta} \in [0.5725, 0.6004]$; $\theta{=}0.60$ falls within this range, and 8/9 held-out predictions match the original $\Kempirical$ (the single mismatch is the borderline rewrite-mode configuration; Table~\ref{tab:theta_lofo}).
ArXiv corroborates with 6/6 LOFO agreement; Wikipedia is underdetermined because most models produce near-chance 1v2 AUC, invalidating the gap-based derivation (Appendix~\ref{sec:theta_lofo}).


\subsection{Features and Classifier}
\label{sec:features}

Each document is characterized by a 15-dimensional feature vector spanning four groups: \emph{surprisal moments} (mean, std, skewness, kurtosis; 4~dims), \emph{surprisal derivatives} (mean and std of first- and second-order differences, plus first-order skewness; 5~dims), \emph{vocabulary diversity} (type-token ratio, hapax legomena ratio, self-BLEU; 3~dims), and \emph{frequency tail statistics} (frequency kurtosis, entropy, rare token fraction; 3~dims).
All features are computed from token-level surprisal values via an external scorer model (full definitions in Table~\ref{tab:s5_features}, Appendix).
Self-BLEU is computed within each CV fold using only same-fold, same-depth reference samples to prevent leakage; it ranks \#1 in 1/8 conditions (greedy decoding) but is absent from the top-3 in all 7 others.
Removing self-BLEU reduces mean $\auc_{1v2}$ by $< 1$\,pp across all models (14D $\Kempirical = 2$ for all 4 configurations; bootstrap CIs in Table~\ref{tab:selfbleu_ablation}); in deployment where depth labels are unavailable, self-BLEU can be replaced with corpus-level self-similarity or omitted with minimal performance loss.
Hand-crafted features enable cross-generator transfer without retraining and permit attribution of discriminative power to specific text properties.

We use \emph{Ordinal Binary Decomposition} (OBD), decomposing the $(K{+}1)$-class problem into $K$ cumulative binary sub-classifiers, each estimating $P(\text{depth} > k \mid \mathbf{x})$ via LightGBM~\cite{ke2017lightgbm} (hyperparameters in Table~\ref{tab:s6_lgbm_params}).
OBD achieves lower MAE than multiclass LightGBM (e.g., 0.984 vs.\ 1.016 on Qwen-rewrite) while maintaining superior pairwise $\auc$ (mean 0.6095 vs.\ 0.4883 for ordinal logistic regression).

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:experimental_setup}

We evaluate ten configurations spanning six architecture families (Table~\ref{tab:setup}): Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (rewrite and continuation modes), Qwen2.5-1.5B (base, continuation), Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-14B, Pythia-1.4B, OLMo-1B, Gemma-2-2B, LLaMA-3.1-8B, and Mistral-7B (all continuation except Qwen-rw).
Each uses 5{,}000 C4~\cite{raffel2020t5} seeds truncated to 256 tokens, recursively generated for $K{=}5$ iterations (30{,}000 documents per configuration).
Default decoding: nucleus $p{=}0.95$, $T{=}1.0$; decoding ablation covers greedy, $T{=}0.7$, and $T{=}1.2$.
Continuation mode truncates seeds to 128 tokens and extends to 256; rewrite mode paraphrases the full text.
Evaluation: 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation grouped by seed document; pairwise $\auc$ as primary metric.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small

\section{Method}
\label{sec:method}

\subsection{Problem Formulation}
\label{sec:formulation}

A generation operator $G_\delta$ (LLM + decoding strategy $\delta$) produces successive generations $X \to Y_1 \to \cdots \to Y_K$, where $Y_k = G_\delta(Y_{k-1})$ and $Y_0 \triangleq X$ (Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).
This sequence forms a Markov chain.
By the Data Processing Inequality, $I(X; Y_1) \geq I(X; Y_2) \geq \cdots \geq 0$: the original signal degrades monotonically.
Together with Markov chain convergence, this motivates a finite $\Ktheory$ beyond which adjacent generations become indistinguishable; DPI guarantees existence but does not bound $\Ktheory$.
Specifically, DPI constrains the cumulative divergence from the seed text; the adjacent-pair convergence that determines $\Kempirical$ follows from the chain's approach to its stationary distribution, where successive transition distributions become indistinguishable.
The actual saturation depth must therefore be measured empirically.

We define the operational lower bound $K^*_{\text{empirical}}$ (hereafter $\Kempirical$):
\begin{equation}
  \Kempirical = \max\!\bigl\{k \!\geq\! 1 : \mathrm{CI}_{\mathrm{low}}(\auc_{j\text{-}1,j}) > \theta,\ \forall j \!\leq\! k\bigr\},
  \label{eq:kstar}
\end{equation}
where $\mathrm{CI}_{\mathrm{low}}(\auc_{k-1,k})$ is the lower bound of a 95\% bootstrap confidence interval (1{,}000 resamples\footnote{Boundary-pair results in Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci} use 1{,}000 resamples; arXiv cross-scorer CIs (Table~\ref{tab:arxiv_crossscorer_ci}) use 10{,}000 for tighter bounds at the margin.}) over the pairwise AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) between depths $k{-}1$ and $k$, and $\theta = 0.60$ is a post-hoc operational threshold (motivated below).
This criterion ensures that $\Kempirical$ reflects statistically robust discriminability rather than sampling noise; the $\forall j \leq k$ constraint is naturally satisfied because $\auc_{k,k+1}$ decreases monotonically for all pairs above $\theta$ across all tested configurations; negligible fluctuations ($\Delta < 0.02$) occur only at deeper depths where discrimination approaches chance level (Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci}).
Since 0v1 $\auc > \theta$ in all tested configurations, $\Kempirical \geq 1$; $\Kempirical{=}0$ (undetectable first-generation text) is not observed.
$\Kempirical$ is an operational quantity jointly conditioned on the feature set and threshold $\theta$; the domain ordering is stable across $\theta \in [0.575, 0.65]$ (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}), though absolute $\Kempirical$ values shift with $\theta$.
We additionally verify that non-boundary-pair CI upper bounds fall below $\theta$ (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}).

\paragraph{Threshold choice.}
We set $\theta{=}0.60$ as a post-hoc operational threshold, chosen at the empirical discontinuity in the AUC distribution (Figure~\ref{fig:kstar_theta}).
A 10{,}000-iteration permutation test yields a 95th-percentile null of ${<}\,0.55$ and $p < 0.002$ for all boundary comparisons, placing $\theta{=}0.60$ well above the empirical null.
$\Kempirical{=}2$ is stable across $\theta \in [0.55, 0.65]$ for all but two marginal configurations (Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci_extended}): 1v2 AUC values cluster at $0.61$--$0.70$ while 2v3 values cluster at $0.55$--$0.59$, creating a ${\sim}$5--11\,pp discontinuity.
Only at extremes does $\Kempirical$ shift: $\theta{=}0.55$ yields $\Kempirical{=}3$ for two Qwen configurations; $\theta{=}0.70$ yields $\Kempirical{=}1$ across all configurations.
The downstream filtering evaluation (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}) uses the OBD classifier without re-optimizing $\theta$, avoiding circularity.
A leave-one-family-out (LOFO) cross-validation on C4 provides an internal consistency check (not external validation): each of five folds derives $\hat{\theta}$ from the gap midpoint between $\min(\auc_{1v2})$ and $\max(\auc_{2v3})$ over the remaining families, yielding $\hat{\theta} \in [0.5725, 0.6004]$; $\theta{=}0.60$ falls within this range, and 8/9 held-out predictions match the original $\Kempirical$ (the single mismatch is the borderline rewrite-mode configuration; Table~\ref{tab:theta_lofo}).
ArXiv corroborates with 6/6 LOFO agreement; Wikipedia is underdetermined because most models produce near-chance 1v2 AUC, invalidating the gap-based derivation (Appendix~\ref{sec:theta_lofo}).


\subsection{Features and Classifier}
\label{sec:features}

Each document is characterized by a 15-dimensional feature vector spanning four groups: \emph{surprisal moments} (mean, std, skewness, kurtosis; 4~dims), \emph{surprisal derivatives} (mean and std of first- and second-order differences, plus first-order skewness; 5~dims), \emph{vocabulary diversity} (type-token ratio, hapax legomena ratio, self-BLEU; 3~dims), and \emph{frequency tail statistics} (frequency kurtosis, entropy, rare token fraction; 3~dims).
All features are computed from token-level surprisal values via an external scorer model (full definitions in Table~\ref{tab:s5_features}, Appendix).
Self-BLEU is computed within each CV fold using only same-fold, same-depth reference samples to prevent leakage; it ranks \#1 in 1/8 conditions (greedy decoding) but is absent from the top-3 in all 7 others.
Removing self-BLEU reduces mean $\auc_{1v2}$ by $< 1$\,pp across all models (14D $\Kempirical = 2$ for all 4 configurations; bootstrap CIs in Table~\ref{tab:selfbleu_ablation}); in deployment where depth labels are unavailable, self-BLEU can be replaced with corpus-level self-similarity or omitted with minimal performance loss.
Hand-crafted features enable cross-generator transfer without retraining and permit attribution of discriminative power to specific text properties.

We use \emph{Ordinal Binary Decomposition} (OBD), decomposing the $(K{+}1)$-class problem into $K$ cumulative binary sub-classifiers, each estimating $P(\text{depth} > k \mid \mathbf{x})$ via LightGBM~\cite{ke2017lightgbm} (hyperparameters in Table~\ref{tab:s6_lgbm_params}).
OBD achieves lower MAE than multiclass LightGBM (e.g., 0.984 vs.\ 1.016 on Qwen-rewrite) while maintaining superior pairwise $\auc$ (mean 0.6095 vs.\ 0.4883 for ordinal logistic regression).

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:experimental_setup}

We evaluate ten configurations spanning six architecture families (Table~\ref{tab:setup}): Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (rewrite and continuation modes), Qwen2.5-1.5B (base, continuation), Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-14B, Pythia-1.4B, OLMo-1B, Gemma-2-2B, LLaMA-3.1-8B, and Mistral-7B (all continuation except Qwen-rw).
Each uses 5{,}000 C4~\cite{raffel2020t5} seeds truncated to 256 tokens, recursively generated for $K{=}5$ iterations (30{,}000 documents per configuration).
Default decoding: nucleus $p{=}0.95$, $T{=}1.0$; decoding ablation covers greedy, $T{=}0.7$, and $T{=}1.2$.
Continuation mode truncates seeds to 128 tokens and extends to 256; rewrite mode paraphrases the full text.
Evaluation: 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation grouped by seed document; pairwise $\auc$ as primary metric.

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

Under prompt-chain recursion ($\leq$32B), the $\theta$-invariant domain ordering arXiv ($\Kempirical{=}3$) $>$ C4 ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $=$ Code ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $>$ Wikipedia ($\Kempirical{=}1$) holds across 7/9 continuation-mode configurations (4/6 families); multi-source pooling preserves domain-calibrated ceilings across all four domains.
DeBERTa matches OBD on low-complexity domains but extends $\Kempirical$ by $+1$ on Wikipedia and arXiv, establishing a feature-set-dependent two-tier structure.
Retrain-chain experiments confirm $\Kempirical{\geq}4$ across three architecture families, placing prompt-chain $\Kempirical{=}2$ as the text-intrinsic floor and retrain-chain $\Kempirical{=}7$ as the protocol-dependent upper bound.

These results yield concrete guidance for corpus curation: binary filtering (remove all $\text{depth} \geq 1$) is the principled choice for web text and code ($\Kempirical \leq 2$), while academic text ($\Kempirical{=}3$) may benefit from finer depth stratification.
$\Kempirical$ localizes where depth-aware filtering yields diminishing returns, preventing practitioners from investing in graduated schemes beyond the discrimination boundary.
The framework is extensible: new domains, models, or feature sets can be evaluated by rerunning the OBD pipeline without architectural changes.

For the model collapse community, $\Kempirical \leq 3$ under generator-independent features implies that population-level quality metrics (TTR decline, mode narrowing) carry the most diagnostic value in the first two to three generations; monitoring beyond this point is unlikely to reveal additional degradation structure.
Open directions include scaling beyond 32B (where the trend toward $\Kempirical{=}1$ may accelerate), characterizing mixed prompt/retrain chains that better approximate real-world contamination, and exploring richer feature representations that may push $\Kempirical$ higher on structured domains.

We additionally verify that non-boundary-pair CI upper bounds fall below $\theta$ (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}).

\paragraph{Threshold choice.}
We set $\theta{=}0.60$ as a post-hoc operational threshold, chosen at the empirical discontinuity in the AUC distribution (Figure~\ref{fig:kstar_theta}).
A 10{,}000-iteration permutation test yields a 95th-percentile null of ${<}\,0.55$ and $p < 0.002$ for all boundary comparisons, placing $\theta{=}0.60$ well above the empirical null.
$\Kempirical{=}2$ is stable across $\theta \in [0.55, 0.65]$ for all but two marginal configurations (Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci_extended}): 1v2 AUC values cluster at $0.61$--$0.70$ while 2v3 values cluster at $0.55$--$0.59$, creating a ${\sim}$5--11\,pp discontinuity.
Only at extremes does $\Kempirical$ shift: $\theta{=}0.55$ yields $\Kempirical{=}3$ for two Qwen configurations; $\theta{=}0.70$ yields $\Kempirical{=}1$ across all configurations.
The downstream filtering evaluation (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}) uses the OBD classifier without re-optimizing $\theta$, avoiding circularity.
A leave-one-family-out (LOFO) cross-validation on C4 provides an internal consistency check (not external validation): each of five folds derives $\hat{\theta}$ from the gap midpoint between $\min(\auc_{1v2})$ and $\max(\auc_{2v3})$ over the remaining families, yielding $\hat{\theta} \in [0.5725, 0.6004]$; $\theta{=}0.60$ falls within this range, and 8/9 held-out predictions match the original $\Kempirical$ (the single mismatch is the borderline rewrite-mode configuration; Table~\ref{tab:theta_lofo}).
ArXiv corroborates with 6/6 LOFO agreement; Wikipedia is underdetermined because most models produce near-chance 1v2 AUC, invalidating the gap-based derivation (Appendix~\ref{sec:theta_lofo}).

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Web-scale text corpora are increasingly contaminated by synthetic content that has itself been generated from earlier synthetic content.
Estimates suggest that a substantial fraction of online text is machine-generated~\cite{sun2025aigt, spennemann2025quantifying}, and this share continues to rise.
When synthetic text is recursively fed back as input, the resulting multi-generational content degrades with each iteration: tail modes vanish, lexical diversity contracts, and surprisal distributions flatten~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, dohmatob2024model}.
This degradation arises in both \emph{retrain-chains} (iteratively training on model outputs) and \emph{prompt-chains} (recursively prompting a fixed model to generate from its own prior outputs); we study prompt-chains, which isolate text-intrinsic information loss from training dynamics (Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_limitations}).
Yet the dominant paradigm treats all machine-generated text identically and ignores the generational depth dimension.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/pipeline.pdf}
\caption{Generational depth estimation pipeline. Seed documents are recursively passed through a generation operator $G_\delta$ to produce a depth chain. Statistical features are fed to the OBD-LightGBM classifier for depth prediction.}
\label{fig:pipeline}
\end{figure*}

This gap cuts across multiple communities.
Binary detectors~\cite{basani2026diveye, zhang2024minkpp} produce no depth estimate (Section~\ref{sec:binary_confidence}).
Membership inference~\cite{zawalski2026codec} addresses a different question, and the model collapse literature~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, alemohammad2024selfconsuming, schaeffer2025position} provides no per-text tool.
Data selection methods~\cite{xie2023dsir, tirumala2023d4, drayson2025} likewise ignore recursive depth.
No existing method estimates how many rounds of recursive generation a text has undergone.

Knowing whether the discriminable depth is finite, and where it saturates, has direct practical consequences.
For data curation, the saturation point determines filtering granularity: if discrimination collapses at depth 2, graduated weighting beyond that boundary injects noise, and binary filtering becomes the principled choice.
Model collapse theory predicts monotonic quality degradation across generations, but existing analyses are population-level and provide no per-text measure of where degradation saturates.
$\Kempirical$ fills this gap by localizing the generation at which adjacent outputs become empirically indistinguishable.

The Data Processing Inequality guarantees monotonic cumulative information loss across generations; together with Markov chain convergence (adjacent transitions $Y_{k-1} \to Y_k$ become increasingly similar as the chain approaches stationarity), this motivates a finite discrimination boundary $\Kstar$, whose actual value must be determined empirically.
We deliberately employ simple, interpretable features to establish a conservative lower bound on the discrimination boundary: any more expressive classifier can only raise $\Kempirical$.
The DeBERTa results (Section~\ref{sec:neural_probe}) confirm this design: neural representations push $\Kempirical$ higher on structured domains, validating the lower-bound interpretation and demonstrating that our measurements are not artifacts of weak classifiers.
We present an empirical characterization study that formalizes $\Kempirical$ (the maximum depth at which a classifier reliably distinguishes adjacent generations) and measures it under prompt-chain generation using 15 statistical features computed via a fixed reference scorer (Section~\ref{sec:features}) and an Ordinal Binary Decomposition (OBD) LightGBM classifier.
We operationalize $\Kempirical$ as the deepest $k \geq 1$ where the pairwise $\auc_{k-1,k}$ exceeds $\theta = 0.60$ (Section~\ref{sec:formulation}).

Our contributions:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
  \item \textbf{First empirical measurement of $\Kempirical$} across 10 model configurations (6 architecture families, 1B--14B), 4 source domains (3 text + 1 code), and 4 decoding strategies at $\theta{=}0.60$: 4/6 families (7/9 continuation-mode configurations) yield $\Kempirical{=}2$ on C4 ($p \leq 0.002$; Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}); multi-source pooling preserves domain-calibrated $\Kempirical$ across all four domains ($+0.008$ $\auc$ for generator identity).
  Zero-shot frontier LLMs likewise collapse beyond $\Kempirical$: per-depth recall at depths $\geq 2$ ranges from 8--38\% (vs.\ 20\% chance), indicating error redistribution rather than genuine depth recovery (Section~\ref{sec:why_kstar}).
  \item \textbf{Domain ordering}: arXiv ($\Kempirical{=}3$) $>$ C4 ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $=$ Code ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $>$ Wikipedia ($\Kempirical{=}1$) holds across tested configurations; code (Python) matches web text depth despite a different modality, confirmed by multi-source pooling (Section~\ref{sec:cross_domain}).
  \item \textbf{Transfer and consistency check}: largely generator-independent features within continuation mode enable 80--92\% accuracy retention among tested configurations ($\rho > 0.90$; Section~\ref{sec:transfer}), though boundary-level $\Kempirical$ assignments are fragile under cross-model transfer (4/6 off-diagonal 7B pairs fall below $\theta$); as a consistency check, domain-appropriate $\Kempirical$ correctly predicts binary ${>}$ graduated filtering for web text (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}).
\end{enumerate}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Web-scale text corpora are increasingly contaminated by synthetic content that has itself been generated from earlier synthetic content.
Estimates suggest that a substantial fraction of online text is machine-generated~\cite{sun2025aigt, spennemann2025quantifying}, and this share continues to rise.
When synthetic text is recursively fed back as input, the resulting multi-generational content degrades with each iteration: tail modes vanish, lexical diversity contracts, and surprisal distributions flatten~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, dohmatob2024model}.
This degradation arises in both \emph{retrain-chains} (iteratively training on model outputs) and \emph{prompt-chains} (recursively prompting a fixed model to generate from its own prior outputs); we study prompt-chains, which isolate text-intrinsic information loss from training dynamics (Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_limitations}).
Yet the dominant paradigm treats all machine-generated text identically and ignores the generational depth dimension.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/pipeline.pdf}
\caption{Generational depth estimation pipeline. Seed documents are recursively passed through a generation operator $G_\delta$ to produce a depth chain. Statistical features are fed to the OBD-LightGBM classifier for depth prediction.}
\label{fig:pipeline}
\end{figure*}

This gap cuts across multiple communities: binary detectors~\cite{basani2026diveye, zhang2024minkpp} produce no depth estimate (Section~\ref{sec:binary_confidence}), membership inference~\cite{zawalski2026codec} addresses a different question, and data selection methods~\cite{xie2023dsir, tirumala2023d4, drayson2025} ignore recursive depth.
No existing method estimates how many rounds of recursive generation a text has undergone.

Knowing whether the discriminable depth is finite, and where it saturates, has direct practical consequences.
For data curation, the saturation point determines filtering granularity: if discrimination collapses at depth 2, graduated weighting beyond that boundary injects noise, and binary filtering becomes the principled choice.
Model collapse theory predicts monotonic quality degradation across generations, but existing analyses are population-level and provide no per-text measure of where degradation saturates.
$\Kempirical$ fills this gap by localizing the generation at which adjacent outputs become empirically indistinguishable.

The Data Processing Inequality guarantees monotonic cumulative information loss across generations; together with Markov chain convergence (adjacent transitions $Y_{k-1} \to Y_k$ become increasingly similar as the chain approaches stationarity), this motivates a finite discrimination boundary $\Kstar$, whose actual value must be determined empirically.
We deliberately employ simple, interpretable features to establish a conservative lower bound on the discrimination boundary: any more expressive classifier can only raise $\Kempirical$.
The DeBERTa results (Section~\ref{sec:neural_probe}) confirm this design: neural representations push $\Kempirical$ higher on structured domains, validating the lower-bound interpretation and demonstrating that our measurements are not artifacts of weak classifiers.
We present an empirical characterization study that formalizes $\Kempirical$ (the maximum depth at which a classifier reliably distinguishes adjacent generations) and measures it under prompt-chain generation using 15 statistical features computed via a fixed reference scorer (Section~\ref{sec:features}) and an Ordinal Binary Decomposition (OBD) LightGBM classifier.
We operationalize $\Kempirical$ as the deepest $k \geq 1$ where the pairwise $\auc_{k-1,k}$ exceeds $\theta = 0.60$ (Section~\ref{sec:formulation}).

Our contributions:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
  \item \textbf{First empirical measurement of $\Kempirical$} across 10 model configurations (6 architecture families, 1B--14B), 4 source domains (3 text + 1 code), and 4 decoding strategies at $\theta{=}0.60$: 4/6 families (7/9 continuation-mode configurations) yield $\Kempirical{=}2$ on C4 ($p \leq 0.002$; Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}); multi-source pooling preserves domain-calibrated $\Kempirical$ across all four domains ($+0.008$ $\auc$ for generator identity).
  Zero-shot frontier LLMs likewise collapse beyond $\Kempirical$: per-depth recall at depths $\geq 2$ ranges from 8--38\% (vs.\ 20\% chance), indicating error redistribution rather than genuine depth recovery (Section~\ref{sec:why_kstar}).
  \item \textbf{Domain ordering}: arXiv ($\Kempirical{=}3$) $>$ C4 ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $=$ Code ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $>$ Wikipedia ($\Kempirical{=}1$) holds across tested configurations; code (Python) matches web text depth despite a different modality, confirmed by multi-source pooling (Section~\ref{sec:cross_domain}).
  \item \textbf{Transfer and consistency check}: largely generator-independent features within continuation mode enable 80--92\% accuracy retention among tested configurations ($\rho > 0.90$; Section~\ref{sec:transfer}), though boundary-level $\Kempirical$ assignments are fragile under cross-model transfer (4/6 off-diagonal 7B pairs fall below $\theta$); as a consistency check, domain-appropriate $\Kempirical$ correctly predicts binary ${>}$ graduated filtering for web text (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}).
\end{enumerate}

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

Under prompt-chain recursion ($\leq$32B), the $\theta$-invariant domain ordering arXiv ($\Kempirical{=}3$) $>$ C4 ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $=$ Code ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $>$ Wikipedia ($\Kempirical{=}1$) holds across 7/9 continuation-mode configurations (4/6 families); multi-source pooling preserves domain-calibrated ceilings across all four domains.
DeBERTa matches OBD on low-complexity domains but extends $\Kempirical$ by $+1$ on Wikipedia and arXiv, establishing a feature-set-dependent two-tier structure.
Retrain-chain experiments confirm $\Kempirical{\geq}4$ across three architecture families, placing prompt-chain $\Kempirical{=}2$ as the text-intrinsic floor and retrain-chain $\Kempirical{=}7$ as the protocol-dependent upper bound.

These results yield concrete guidance for corpus curation: binary filtering (remove all $\text{depth} \geq 1$) is the principled choice for web text and code ($\Kempirical \leq 2$), while academic text ($\Kempirical{=}3$) may benefit from finer depth stratification.
$\Kempirical$ localizes where depth-aware filtering yields diminishing returns, preventing practitioners from investing in graduated schemes beyond the discrimination boundary.
The framework is extensible: new domains, models, or feature sets can be evaluated by rerunning the OBD pipeline without architectural changes.

For the model collapse community, $\Kempirical \leq 3$ under generator-independent features implies that population-level quality metrics (TTR decline, mode narrowing) carry the most diagnostic value in the first two to three generations; monitoring beyond this point is unlikely to reveal additional degradation structure.
Open directions include scaling beyond 32B (where the trend toward $\Kempirical{=}1$ may accelerate), characterizing mixed prompt/retrain chains that better approximate real-world contamination, and exploring richer feature representations that may push $\Kempirical$ higher on structured domains.

4	\subsection{Problem Formulation}
5	\label{sec:formulation}
6	
7	A generation operator $G_\delta$ (LLM + decoding strategy $\delta$) produces successive generations $X \to Y_1 \to \cdots \to Y_K$, where $Y_k = G_\delta(Y_{k-1})$ and $Y_0 \triangleq X$ (Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).
8	This sequence forms a Markov chain.
9	By the Data Processing Inequality, $I(X; Y_1) \geq I(X; Y_2) \geq \cdots \geq 0$: the original signal degrades monotonically.
10	Together with Markov chain convergence, this motivates a finite $\Ktheory$ beyond which adjacent generations become indistinguishable; DPI guarantees existence but does not bound $\Ktheory$.
11	Specifically, DPI constrains the cumulative divergence from the seed text; the adjacent-pair convergence that determines $\Kempirical$ follows from the chain's approach to its stationary distribution, where successive transition distributions become indistinguishable.
12	The actual saturation depth must therefore be measured empirically.
13	
14	We define the operational lower bound $K^*_{\text{empirical}}$ (hereafter $\Kempirical$):
15	\begin{equation}
16	  \Kempirical = \max\!\bigl\{k \!\geq\! 1 : \mathrm{CI}_{\mathrm{low}}(\auc_{j\text{-}1,j}) > \theta,\ \forall j \!\leq\! k\bigr\},
17	  \label{eq:kstar}
18	\end{equation}
19	where $\mathrm{CI}_{\mathrm{low}}(\auc_{k-1,k})$ is the lower bound of a 95\% bootstrap confidence interval (1{,}000 resamples\footnote{We use 1{,}000 resamples as the default for computational efficiency; arXiv cross-scorer CIs (Table~\ref{tab:arxiv_crossscorer_ci}) use 10{,}000 to achieve tighter bounds at marginal boundaries where sub-pp differences determine the $\Kempirical{=}2$ vs.\ $\Kempirical{=}3$ verdict.}) over the pairwise AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) between depths $k{-}1$ and $k$, and $\theta = 0.60$ is a post-hoc operational threshold (motivated below).
20	This criterion ensures that $\Kempirical$ reflects statistically robust discriminability rather than sampling noise; the $\forall j \leq k$ constraint is naturally satisfied because $\auc_{k,k+1}$ decreases monotonically for all pairs above $\theta$ across all tested configurations; negligible fluctuations ($\Delta < 0.02$) occur only at deeper depths where discrimination approaches chance level (Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci}).
21	Since 0v1 $\auc > \theta$ in all tested configurations, $\Kempirical \geq 1$; $\Kempirical{=}0$ (undetectable first-generation text) is not observed.
22	$\Kempirical$ is an operational quantity jointly conditioned on the feature set and threshold $\theta$; the domain ordering is stable across $\theta \in [0.575, 0.65]$ (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}), though absolute $\Kempirical$ values shift with $\theta$.
23	We additionally verify that non-boundary-pair CI upper bounds fall below $\theta$ (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}).
24	
25	\paragraph{Threshold choice.}
26	We set $\theta{=}0.60$ as a post-hoc operational threshold, chosen at the empirical discontinuity in the AUC distribution (Figure~\ref{fig:kstar_theta}).
27	A 10{,}000-iteration permutation test yields a 95th-percentile null of ${<}\,0.55$ and $p < 0.002$ for all boundary comparisons, placing $\theta{=}0.60$ well above the empirical null.
28	$\Kempirical{=}2$ is stable across $\theta \in [0.55, 0.65]$ for all but two marginal configurations (Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci_extended}): 1v2 AUC values cluster at $0.61$--$0.70$ while 2v3 values cluster at $0.55$--$0.59$, creating a ${\sim}$5--11\,pp discontinuity.
29	Only at extremes does $\Kempirical$ shift: $\theta{=}0.55$ yields $\Kempirical{=}3$ for two Qwen configurations; $\theta{=}0.70$ yields $\Kempirical{=}1$ across all configurations.
30	The downstream filtering evaluation (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}) uses the OBD classifier without re-optimizing $\theta$, avoiding circularity.
31	A leave-one-family-out (LOFO) cross-validation on C4 provides an internal consistency check (not external validation): each of five folds derives $\hat{\theta}$ from the gap midpoint between $\min(\auc_{1v2})$ and $\max(\auc_{2v3})$ over the remaining families, yielding $\hat{\theta} \in [0.5725, 0.6004]$; $\theta{=}0.60$ falls within this range, and 8/9 held-out predictions match the original $\Kempirical$ (the single mismatch is the borderline rewrite-mode configuration; Table~\ref{tab:theta_lofo}).
32	ArXiv corroborates with 6/6 LOFO agreement; Wikipedia is underdetermined because most models produce near-chance 1v2 AUC, invalidating the gap-based derivation (Appendix~\ref{sec:theta_lofo}).
33	
34	
35	\subsection{Features and Classifier}
36	\label{sec:features}
37	
38	Each document is characterized by a 15-dimensional feature vector spanning four groups: \emph{surprisal moments} (mean, std, skewness, kurtosis; 4~dims), \emph{surprisal derivatives} (mean and std of first- and second-order differences, plus first-order skewness; 5~dims), \emph{vocabulary diversity} (type-token ratio, hapax legomena ratio, self-BLEU; 3~dims), and \emph{frequency tail statistics} (frequency kurtosis, entropy, rare token fraction; 3~dims).
39	All features are computed from token-level surprisal values via an external scorer model (full definitions in Table~\ref{tab:s5_features}, Appendix).
40	Self-BLEU is computed within each CV fold using only same-fold, same-depth reference samples to prevent leakage; it ranks \#1 in 1/8 conditions (greedy decoding) but is absent from the top-3 in all 7 others.
41	Removing self-BLEU reduces mean $\auc_{1v2}$ by $< 1$\,pp across all models (14D $\Kempirical = 2$ for all 4 configurations; bootstrap CIs in Table~\ref{tab:selfbleu_ablation}); in deployment where depth labels are unavailable, self-BLEU can be replaced with corpus-level self-similarity or omitted with minimal performance loss.
42	Hand-crafted features enable cross-generator transfer without retraining and permit attribution of discriminative power to specific text properties.
43	
44	We use \emph{Ordinal Binary Decomposition} (OBD), decomposing the $(K{+}1)$-class problem into $K$ cumulative binary sub-classifiers, each estimating $P(\text{depth} > k \mid \mathbf{x})$ via LightGBM~\cite{ke2017lightgbm} (hyperparameters in Table~\ref{tab:s6_lgbm_params}).
45	OBD achieves lower MAE than multiclass LightGBM (e.g., 0.984 vs.\ 1.016 on Qwen-rewrite) while maintaining superior pairwise $\auc$ (mean 0.6095 vs.\ 0.4883 for ordinal logistic regression).
46	
47	\subsection{Experimental Setup}
48	\label{sec:experimental_setup}

50	We evaluate ten configurations spanning six architecture families (Table~\ref{tab:setup}): Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (rewrite and continuation modes), Qwen2.5-1.5B (base, continuation), Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-14B, Pythia-1.4B, OLMo-1B, Gemma-2-2B, LLaMA-3.1-8B, and Mistral-7B (all continuation except Qwen-rw).
51	Each uses 5{,}000 C4~\cite{raffel2020t5} seeds truncated to 256 tokens, recursively generated for $K{=}5$ iterations (30{,}000 documents per configuration).
52	Default decoding: nucleus $p{=}0.95$, $T{=}1.0$; decoding ablation covers greedy, $T{=}0.7$, and $T{=}1.2$.
53	Continuation mode truncates seeds to 128 tokens and extends to 256; rewrite mode paraphrases the full text.
54	Evaluation: 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation grouped by seed document; pairwise $\auc$ as primary metric.

\section{Method}
\label{sec:method}

\subsection{Problem Formulation}
\label{sec:formulation}

A generation operator $G_\delta$ (LLM + decoding strategy $\delta$) produces successive generations $X \to Y_1 \to \cdots \to Y_K$, where $Y_k = G_\delta(Y_{k-1})$ and $Y_0 \triangleq X$ (Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).
This sequence forms a Markov chain.
By the Data Processing Inequality, $I(X; Y_1) \geq I(X; Y_2) \geq \cdots \geq 0$: the original signal degrades monotonically.
Together with Markov chain convergence, this motivates a finite $\Ktheory$ beyond which adjacent generations become indistinguishable; DPI guarantees existence but does not bound $\Ktheory$.
Specifically, DPI constrains the cumulative divergence from the seed text; the adjacent-pair convergence that determines $\Kempirical$ follows from the chain's approach to its stationary distribution, where successive transition distributions become indistinguishable.
The actual saturation depth must therefore be measured empirically.

We define the operational lower bound $K^*_{\text{empirical}}$ (hereafter $\Kempirical$):
\begin{equation}
  \Kempirical = \max\!\bigl\{k \!\geq\! 1 : \mathrm{CI}_{\mathrm{low}}(\auc_{j\text{-}1,j}) > \theta,\ \forall j \!\leq\! k\bigr\},
  \label{eq:kstar}
\end{equation}
where $\mathrm{CI}_{\mathrm{low}}(\auc_{k-1,k})$ is the lower bound of a 95\% bootstrap confidence interval (1{,}000 resamples\footnote{We use 1{,}000 resamples as the default for computational efficiency; arXiv cross-scorer CIs (Table~\ref{tab:arxiv_crossscorer_ci}) use 10{,}000 to achieve tighter bounds at marginal boundaries where sub-pp differences determine the $\Kempirical{=}2$ vs.\ $\Kempirical{=}3$ verdict.}) over the pairwise AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) between depths $k{-}1$ and $k$, and $\theta = 0.60$ is a post-hoc operational threshold (motivated below).
This criterion ensures that $\Kempirical$ reflects statistically robust discriminability rather than sampling noise; the $\forall j \leq k$ constraint is naturally satisfied because $\auc_{k,k+1}$ decreases monotonically for all pairs above $\theta$ across all tested configurations; negligible fluctuations ($\Delta < 0.02$) occur only at deeper depths where discrimination approaches chance level (Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci}).
Since 0v1 $\auc > \theta$ in all tested configurations, $\Kempirical \geq 1$; $\Kempirical{=}0$ (undetectable first-generation text) is not observed.
$\Kempirical$ is an operational quantity jointly conditioned on the feature set and threshold $\theta$; the domain ordering is stable across $\theta \in [0.575, 0.65]$ (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}), though absolute $\Kempirical$ values shift with $\theta$.
We additionally verify that non-boundary-pair CI upper bounds fall below $\theta$ (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}).

\paragraph{Threshold choice.}
We set $\theta{=}0.60$ as a post-hoc operational threshold, chosen at the empirical discontinuity in the AUC distribution (Figure~\ref{fig:kstar_theta}).
A 10{,}000-iteration permutation test yields a 95th-percentile null of ${<}\,0.55$ and $p < 0.002$ for all boundary comparisons, placing $\theta{=}0.60$ well above the empirical null.
$\Kempirical{=}2$ is stable across $\theta \in [0.55, 0.65]$ for all but two marginal configurations (Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci_extended}): 1v2 AUC values cluster at $0.61$--$0.70$ while 2v3 values cluster at $0.55$--$0.59$, creating a ${\sim}$5--11\,pp discontinuity.
Only at extremes does $\Kempirical$ shift: $\theta{=}0.55$ yields $\Kempirical{=}3$ for two Qwen configurations; $\theta{=}0.70$ yields $\Kempirical{=}1$ across all configurations.
The downstream filtering evaluation (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}) uses the OBD classifier without re-optimizing $\theta$, avoiding circularity.
A leave-one-family-out (LOFO) cross-validation on C4 provides an internal consistency check (not external validation): each of five folds derives $\hat{\theta}$ from the gap midpoint between $\min(\auc_{1v2})$ and $\max(\auc_{2v3})$ over the remaining families, yielding $\hat{\theta} \in [0.5725, 0.6004]$; $\theta{=}0.60$ falls within this range, and 8/9 held-out predictions match the original $\Kempirical$ (the single mismatch is the borderline rewrite-mode configuration; Table~\ref{tab:theta_lofo}).
ArXiv corroborates with 6/6 LOFO agreement; Wikipedia is underdetermined because most models produce near-chance 1v2 AUC, invalidating the gap-based derivation (Appendix~\ref{sec:theta_lofo}).


\subsection{Features and Classifier}
\label{sec:features}

Each document is characterized by a 15-dimensional feature vector spanning four groups: \emph{surprisal moments} (mean, std, skewness, kurtosis; 4~dims), \emph{surprisal derivatives} (mean and std of first- and second-order differences, plus first-order skewness; 5~dims), \emph{vocabulary diversity} (type-token ratio, hapax legomena ratio, self-BLEU; 3~dims), and \emph{frequency tail statistics} (frequency kurtosis, entropy, rare token fraction; 3~dims).
All features are computed from token-level surprisal values via an external scorer model (full definitions in Table~\ref{tab:s5_features}, Appendix).
Self-BLEU is computed within each CV fold using only same-fold, same-depth reference samples to prevent leakage; it ranks \#1 in 1/8 conditions (greedy decoding) but is absent from the top-3 in all 7 others.
Removing self-BLEU reduces mean $\auc_{1v2}$ by $< 1$\,pp across all models (14D $\Kempirical = 2$ for all 4 configurations; bootstrap CIs in Table~\ref{tab:selfbleu_ablation}); in deployment where depth labels are unavailable, self-BLEU can be replaced with corpus-level self-similarity or omitted with minimal performance loss.
Hand-crafted features enable cross-generator transfer without retraining and permit attribution of discriminative power to specific text properties.

We use \emph{Ordinal Binary Decomposition} (OBD), decomposing the $(K{+}1)$-class problem into $K$ cumulative binary sub-classifiers, each estimating $P(\text{depth} > k \mid \mathbf{x})$ via LightGBM~\cite{ke2017lightgbm} (hyperparameters in Table~\ref{tab:s6_lgbm_params}).
OBD achieves lower MAE than multiclass LightGBM (e.g., 0.984 vs.\ 1.016 on Qwen-rewrite) while maintaining superior pairwise $\auc$ (mean 0.6095 vs.\ 0.4883 for ordinal logistic regression).

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:experimental_setup}

We evaluate ten configurations spanning six architecture families (Table~\ref{tab:setup}): Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (rewrite and continuation modes), Qwen2.5-1.5B (base, continuation), Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-14B, Pythia-1.4B, OLMo-1B, Gemma-2-2B, LLaMA-3.1-8B, and Mistral-7B (all continuation except Qwen-rw).
Each uses 5{,}000 C4~\cite{raffel2020t5} seeds truncated to 256 tokens, recursively generated for $K{=}5$ iterations (30{,}000 documents per configuration).
Default decoding: nucleus $p{=}0.95$, $T{=}1.0$; decoding ablation covers greedy, $T{=}0.7$, and $T{=}1.2$.
Continuation mode truncates seeds to 128 tokens and extends to 256; rewrite mode paraphrases the full text.
Evaluation: 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation grouped by seed document; pairwise $\auc$ as primary metric.
